observation.visible_scene: Nighttime outdoor setting. A person seen from behind, bare-backed with a small tattoo on the upper back/shoulder blade and long pale gloves on both arms, holds two fan-shaped wire-frame props (each a curved arc with several radiating spokes) raised overhead. Flames burn at the tips of the spokes and emit rising smoke. Background left: a stone staircase with white balusters and a seated dark cat; background right: green palm- and pine-like foliage against a dark sky.
visible_changes: The flames at the spoke tips flicker and change shape continuously throughout, with smoke plumes drifting upward and varying in density.

The orientation of both fan structures rotates/tilts over the segment: the right fan's arc shifts from a steep diagonal (spokes pointing up-left to right) toward a flatter, more horizontal arc near the top, and the left fan likewise reorients, indicating the performer is turning the fans in their hands rather than the fans translating across the frame.
The performer's arms stay raised overhead the whole time, with only small changes in wrist/elbow angle as the fans are manipulated.

The framing gradually shows more of the upper flame arc and the person's head sits lower in the frame by the end, consistent with a slight upward camera tilt and/or the performer lifting the props higher.
The cat on the stairs remains seated and largely static; the foliage and balusters persist as background.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fan-rotation is part of a larger choreography that began before or continues after this excerpt.
The performer's face, front of body, and full routine.
What causes the smoke/flame intensity variations (fuel, wind, manipulation).
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the change in framing is camera tilt/zoom or the performer raising their arms; both could contribute.
The exact degree of fan spin (full rotation vs. partial tilt) cannot be confirmed from the sampled frames.
Material identity of the props and flames (e.g., fuel type) is not visible.
